### LOW: Threat model does not cover newly persisted cache\-routing state \(holders and observed demand\)
[CHANGELOG\.md:395](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/17189b1810154df65659966ea55dc51dcd6b6f89/CHANGELOG.md#L395) · T-041, T-059

The changelog says the coordinator now writes SSD cache holders and observed per\-prefix demand to the database and restores them after restart\. T\-041 and SEC\-035 only reason about provider\-side SSD artifacts and in\-process routing state\. A new durable store is not covered: its contents \(HMAC\-derived scope and prefix identifiers, provider bindings, demand counts\), its retention, and its exposure through admin or DB access and the \`GET /v1/cache/status\` persistence fields\. The stated limitations \(crashes before the reset marker, concurrent coordinator writers\) mean stale or cross\-session holders could survive an invalidation\. A holder surviving a proof mismatch or fence would route a request to a provider that no longer holds the checkpoint, which causes misrouting and a wrong demand signal rather than a confidentiality break\. The new store extends the SEC\-035 timing\-oracle window across coordinator restarts\. Fix: add the persisted routing store as a T\-041 asset or sub\-threat, with its retention and TTL, key rotation via cache\-key generation, deletion on account erasure \(T\-059\), and the limitations above\. Confirm that no raw chain hashes or account identifiers are stored\.

### LOW: Stripe payout migration adds credentials and a webhook verification path not reflected in TB\-008
[CHANGELOG\.md:262](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/17189b1810154df65659966ea55dc51dcd6b6f89/CHANGELOG.md#L262) · A-009, T-030

The Global Payouts cutover separates legacy Connect credentials from Checkout, adds connected\-account webhook verification, and recovers rejected\-transfer refunds atomically\. This adds Stripe secrets, a webhook endpoint with its own signing secret, and ledger\-affecting refund repair\. T\-030 covers duplicate Checkout webhooks and A\-009 covers the ledger, but neither anticipates the extra credentials, the verified\-refund crediting path, or the operator\-run historical refund repair tool\. A wrong or unverified event on that path could credit balances twice or divert payouts\. Fix: update TB\-008 and T\-030 to cover per\-endpoint signature verification, idempotency for refund and transfer\-rejection events, secret storage and rotation for the legacy credentials, and authorization and audit of the refund\-repair and audit tooling\. Source was not supplied, so this is a threat\-model gap rather than a confirmed defect\.
